entries.title: Numbers 1:1
segments: The second month; called Zif; answering to the last part of April and the first part of May.

entries.title: Numbers 1:2
segments: Take ye the sum of all the congregation; the Hebrew civil division was into thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens,

and this served also as the basis of the military division, 1Sa 8.12; 22.7.  The present numbering was an enrolment of the men of war in regular military array.  A numbering had been made of the people a few months before.

.  The tables prepared on that occasion seem to have served for the present enrolment, the men appointed to oversee it simply filling up the vacancies occasioned by death from those who had in the meanwhile reached the age of twenty years.  Hence the sum is in both cases the same, namely, six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty. It is to be noticed further,that with the single exception of the tribe of Gad,
, no divisions lower than hundreds are reckoned.

entries.title: Numbers 1:16
segments: Renowned of the congregation; rather, "the called of the congregation;" that is, men of standing and influence, who were regularly called to the assemblies of the people; for these assemblies consisted not of the whole mass of the people, but of certain representatives from each family.

entries.title: Numbers 1:18
segments: Their pedigrees; the line of their forefathers.

entries.title: Numbers 1:20
segments:
vv 20-25. 
 
  Reuben--Simeon--Gad; the tribes are grouped in three, according to their encampment, as described in the following chapters, these three tribes having their place on the south side of the tabernacle.

entries.title: Numbers 1:45
segments:
vv 45-46. 
 
  All that were able to go forth to war in Israel--were six hundred thousand; the number able for war shows that the whole people must have amounted to more than two millions.

entries.title: Numbers 1:46
segments: From the great increase of the Israelites in their bondage, and from their deliverance according to the divine prediction, we have evidence of the faithfulness of God, and are encouraged to trust in him for the fulfillment of all his promises.
